what: Orientation audit of the 116 Voyager Golden Record images. Separates what the signal actually encodes from what human recognition supplies.
encodedOrientationNote: Always 0, for every image, as a statement of fact. The record encodes no "this way up" information whatsoever: the signal fixes a raster of 512 traces and nothing about which edge is the top. encodedOrientation is therefore the unrotated decode - the only orientation the signal itself licenses. An alien recipient could not do better than guess.
displayOrientationNote: Our judgement, derived from recognising the subject matter, which is human knowledge and not recoverable from the signal. Expressed as QUARTER TURNS CLOCKWISE applied to the as-encoded frame: 0 = none, 1 = 90 CW, 2 = 180, 3 = 90 CCW (270 CW).
conventionWarning: displayOrientation is NOT in the same convention as currentOrientation. Barry's 2017 column uses 1 and 2 for quarter turns in OPPOSITE directions (1 = 90 CW, 2 = 90 CCW) and has no way to express a half turn. The field currentOrientationAsQuarterTurnsCW restates his value in the display convention so the two can be compared directly; displayOrientation differs from it only where changed is true.
howTheConventionWasFixed: Empirically, from frames whose own hand-lettering settles the answer, not from the code. Barry 1 = 90 CW: L033 (image 26, MALE/FEMALE and every leader label reads left-to-right) and L039 (image 32, 160 cm / 155 cm / 20 y upright, figures standing). Barry 2 = 90 CCW: all four frames that carry the value - L012 Jupiter, L013 Earth, L074 insect, R077 violin - read their own captions upright only after a counter-clockwise quarter turn, and the scanned book plates for Earth, the insect and the violin independently imply the same 3 quarter turns clockwise.
method: Every one of the 116 images was rendered at all four quarter turns from the as-encoded decode (reconstructed by undoing the rotation pipeline/build.py bakes into data/thumbs) and looked at. Colour images were composited from their RGB triplets where that helped. Judgements were then screened against the scanned book plates in docs/reference: 95 images have a plate match at or above 60 RANSAC inliers, and 93 of those confirmed the 2017 table. The two that did not were inspected side by side with the plate and are the two corrections recorded here.

images.title: Calibration circle
images.evidence: A plain dark circle centred on a light field. It is rotationally symmetric: all four quarter turns are identical apart from decode noise along one frame edge, and the reference scan (Jon Lomberg, Wikimedia Commons) is likewise a bare circle with no asymmetric feature. No evidence exists in the frame or in any reference. 0 is recorded as the do-nothing default, not as a determination.

images.title: Solar location map
images.evidence: CORRECTED. The scanned book plate prints the pulsar radiant at upper LEFT with the galaxy inset at lower RIGHT; the as-encoded decode has both exactly reversed. The decisive detail is asymmetric: the small bright companion dot sits to the LEFT of the galaxy's core in the plate and in our 180-rotated decode, and to the RIGHT in the as-encoded frame. So this slide needs a half turn. Barry's column records 0, and being limited to 0/1/2 quarter turns it cannot express a half turn at all. Corroborated by the scanned book plate (page 24, 94 RANSAC inliers), which independently implies 2 quarter turn(s) clockwise from the as-encoded frame.

images.title: Mathematical definitions

images.title: Solar spectrum
images.evidence: Confirmed against the reference scan of the original slide (National Astronomy and Ionosphere Center, Wikimedia Commons): a horizontal dispersed band running blue at the LEFT through green to red at the RIGHT, with a faint X ruled across the green section. Our colour composite of the L007/L008/L009 triplet reproduces that left-right sense exactly, which is what fixes the answer - a horizontal band alone would leave 0 and 180 open.

images.title: Mercury
images.evidence: Confirmed against the reference scan (NASA, Wikimedia Commons): the bright cratered limb sweeps from upper left down to the right with black space above it, matching the as-encoded frame. Corroborated by the scanned book plate (page 27, 425 RANSAC inliers), which independently implies 0 quarter turn(s) clockwise from the as-encoded frame.

images.title: Jupiter
images.evidence: Caption evidence. This is one of the frames that fixes Barry's 2 as a counter-clockwise quarter turn.

images.title: Conception
images.evidence: CORRECTED. The scanned book plate for this micrograph is LANDSCAPE - the grainy ovum fills the right-hand side, the sperm are scattered in the dark field to the left, and a hand-drawn leader line points rightward at a single sperm on the ovum's margin. That is the as-encoded frame exactly, detail for detail, including the second sperm just below-left of the leader tip and the column of sperm down the left edge. Barry's quarter turn puts it portrait with the ovum at the bottom. This was the one image every previous pass called undetermined and kept at 1 only by analogy with the companion diagram (image 27); the plate settles it, and the analogy was misleading. Corroborated by the scanned book plate (page 33, 625 RANSAC inliers), which independently implies 0 quarter turn(s) clockwise from the as-encoded frame.
